classification.difficultyReason: Convert a rational inequality into a cubic comparison while retaining two excluded denominator zeroes.

inlines.text: Multiply by the denominator squared, sketch the resulting cubic, and exclude

answer.worked:
The denominator is $(x+2)(x-1)$, so $x\ne-2,1$. For these values, its square is positive:
$$\begin{align*}(2x^2+1)(x^2+x-2)&\ge2(x^2+x-2)^2\\(x^2+x-2)\bigl[2x^2+1-2(x^2+x-2)\bigr]&\ge0\\(x+2)(x-1)(5-2x)&\ge0.\end{align*}$$
Sketch $y=(x+2)(x-1)(5-2x)$. Its zeroes satisfy
$$\begin{align*}(x+2)(x-1)(5-2x)&=0\\x&=-2,\ 1,\ \frac52.\end{align*}$$
The cubic is on or above the $x$-axis for $x\le-2$ or $1\le x\le\frac52$. Excluding the denominator zeroes gives
$$x<-2\quad\text{or}\quad 1<x\le\frac52.$$

spec.description: Cubic obtained by multiplying the rational inequality by the denominator squared. Open markers distinguish excluded poles from the included equality value.
spec.mathematics: p(x)=(x+2)(x-1)(5-2x). Select p(x)>=0, then exclude x=-2 and x=1.
